topic: The Human Immune System: Innate vs. Adaptive Defense Architecture

slides.title: The Human Immune System: Innate vs. Adaptive Defense Architecture
Innate Immunity: Our First Line of Defense
slides.visual_prompt: An illustration depicting the innate immune system as a rapid, non-specific first line of defense. Show physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes, and cellular components like macrophages and neutrophils engulfing pathogens. Use a clean, modern, and slightly abstract style with a dark background.

slides.title: Adaptive Immunity: Targeted & Memory-Driven Response
slides.visual_prompt: An illustration showcasing the adaptive immune system with T-cells and B-cells. Depict T-cells recognizing infected cells and B-cells producing antibodies. Emphasize specificity and memory, perhaps with a visual representation of memory cells. Use a clean, modern, and slightly abstract style with a dark background.

slides.title: Innate vs. Adaptive: Key Differentiators
slides.visual_prompt: A table infographic visually comparing innate and adaptive immunity. Use icons or simple diagrams to represent key differences like speed (fast vs. slow), specificity (non-specific vs. specific), memory (none vs. yes), and main components (phagocytes vs. lymphocytes). The visual should complement a detailed comparison table.

slides.title: mRNA Vaccines: Precision Delivery & Immune Activation
slides.visual_prompt: An illustration showing the mechanism of mRNA vaccine delivery. Depict mRNA encapsulated within a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) entering a cell, releasing mRNA, and the cell producing viral spike proteins to trigger an immune response. Use a clear, scientific, and modern diagrammatic style with a dark background.

slides.title: CAR-T Cell Therapy: Engineering Immunity Against Cancer
slides.visual_prompt: An illustration demonstrating CAR-T cell therapy. Show T-cells being extracted from a patient, genetically engineered with Chimeric Antigen Receptors (CARs), expanded in vitro, and then re-infused to target and destroy cancer cells. Use a clear, scientific, and modern diagrammatic style with a dark background.
